title: Two-enzyme catalysis-induced condensates with non-reciprocal chemotaxis (e1 chases e2's product, e2 flees e1's) on a consumed fuel: from noise, static e1 droplets and e2 blobs form, and e1-core/e2-crescent composites appear, one of which travels 6 diameters in a straight line; most composites are short-lived
summary: world.py adds a second conserved enzyme to the CIPS world of 20261025T1845-c23-cips-metabolic-claim, with volume filling on e1+e2, self-condensation chi11=chi22=1 and non-reciprocal cross terms chi12=+1, chi21=-1 (Agudo-Canalejo & Golestanian 2019), on the same consumed, regrowing fuel. From uniform e1=e2=0.1 plus noise, bodies form by t~500 (pack/, seed 0, 256^2, t=2500): small static e1 droplets, larger e2 blobs, and composites where an e2 crescent wraps an e1 core (p_base_rg.png, red e1, green e2). labkit on e1+e2 counts 166 tracks moving >= 1 body length (max 3.5), 52 persistent splits (generation 3) and 444 merges: a churning population. In a 128^2 run tracked every 10 t (mover.png), one composite moves 36 px (5.9 diameters) in a straight line over 1000 t with its crescent preserved; the other full-window e1 tracks move a median 0.19 diameters. Stronger cross-coupling (chi12=2, chi21=-2; p_strong_rg.png) turns e2 into a foam whose cells each hold an e1 droplet. A 12-point screen (sweep.txt: cross couplings, self couplings, enzyme ratio, De, kF, DF) found no regime where most composites travel. Not claimed: M is one track, and the composites' lifetimes and the matched reciprocal twin are not measured.
